Thanks again for a productive first sprint. Per our retro this morning I wanted to capture the pragmatic handover items we discussed so Frostline can start operating with the telemetry and runbooks we agreed on. High level items:

- Dashboards: initial SLO & error dashboards + latency P95 by route (dashboard-wireframe attached).
- Tracing hooks: span naming conventions + client-side header propagation (we scoped 5 critical flows).
- Error taxonomy: classify by user-impact vs transient vs infra; map to runbook playbook pages.
- Alert routing: page on-call -> Slack #frostline-ops -> Escalation chain; define noise thresholds.
- Runbooks: Redwood runbook template attached; please adopt and populate for the top three incident classes.

Next steps I propose:
1) Frostline fills the implementation timeline (attached) with any date constraints by Wednesday 21 Jul.
2) We deliver the initial dashboards and tracing hook examples by Friday 23 Jul for review.
3) Ben will share the runbook scaffold and a sample filled play for "model inference OOM".

Attachments: Frostline_implementation_timeline.xlsx, Redwood_Runbook_Template.md, dashboard-wireframe.png

Any additions? If not, I’ll schedule a short checkpoint Friday 23 Jul 10:00 PT.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett

Samir / team — attaching the runbook scaffold and a filled example for "model inference OOM". See Redwood_Runbook_Template.md (attached) and the sample play below.

--- SAMPLE PLAY: model inference OOM ---
Trigger: Container restarts with OOM metric > 0.5 within 5m window
Immediate checks:
- Check service memory usage (kubectl top / metrics)
- Confirm model size and quantization variant currently deployed
Mitigation:
- Roll back to quantized variant (v1.2-q4) via canary route (ops-runbook playbook steps 4-7)
- Recycle pod with graceful drain, preserve KV cache where possible
Communication:
- Post incident summary to #frostline-ops, tag on-call
- If >15min user impact, notify product and CS leads
Postmortem: attach logs, top goroutines, and heap dump to Jira OPS ticket
--- end sample ---

Ben has also pushed a small Python tracing snippet to the Drive link (see related_links). That snippet shows header propagation and span naming conventions. Will follow up with a small PR to your repo if that helps.

Ben Carter
Technical Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Observability implementation: sprint retro, runbook handover & next steps

Hi Samir, Elena — quick follow-up on dashboards and alert routing from the instrumention side.

Dashboard notes:
- We created two starter dashboards: "SLO & Errors (Service)" and "Latency by Route (P50/P95)". They are wireframed in the attached PNG; final will be sent as JSON for your Grafana later this week.
- Suggested panels: 5xx rate (5m/1h), request P95 (by tag), error budget burn rate.

Tracing hooks / instrumentation:
- Span name conventions: service.operation.component (e.g., frostop.infer.predictor.request)
- Client header: X-Redwood-Trace (propagate trace id, parent id). Sample code is on the Drive link.

Alert routing:
- Alert severity mapping: sev1 (user-facing outage) -> page on-call -> Slack #frostline-ops -> phone escalation; sev2 (degraded performance) -> Slack + email to engineering leads.
- We recommend a 10-minute quiet window for retrying upstream transient errors before paging.

I'll upload the Grafana JSON and an initial alert rule set to Jira OPS-9923 by Thu EOD. If you want us to turn those alerts on in your staging workspace, share a service account with Grafana editor rights and we can import.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — that mapping looks good. A few clarifications from engineering after a quick read-through:
- For the quiet retry window, can we set the default to 30s with room to tune per-route? Some downstreams are flakier and 10m could mask issues.
- We prefer the header name to be X-Trace-Redwood to match internal conventions; will Redwood accept that for compatibility?

We will populate the timeline today and share the procurement note to our steering committee. If Redwood can import the staging dashboards on Fri, that would be ideal.
